findings.title: OnWeaponHitCharacter argument order disables the fracture hook
findings.reproduction_evidence: Current engine emits OnWeaponHitCharacter(wielder,target,weapon,damageSplit). The Lua handler declares (attacker,weapon,target), so its target variable receives the weapon; target ~= player is true and line 33 returns before reading UT_fractureMult or rolling.
findings.missing_proof: No missing proof for the static mismatch. No current in-game run demonstrates corrected behavior because product code was not changed.
findings.recommended_correction: Change the callback contract to (attacker,target,weapon,damageSplit) and update mocks/tests to fire the exact engine order.
findings.smallest_regression_test: Register the real handler, fire OnWeaponHitCharacter(attacker,player,weapon,damage) with ZombRand forced to succeed, and assert an eligible player body part fractures.

findings.title: Fracture cooldown counts hits instead of elapsed ticks or time
findings.reproduction_evidence: A successful roll stores 300. The only decrement is inside OnWeaponHitCharacter and subtracts one per later callback. Waiting ten seconds without 300 weapon-hit events leaves the cooldown unchanged; it is a 300-hit cooldown.
findings.missing_proof: No independent tick/time event decrements UT_fractureCooldown in the inspected current hook.
findings.recommended_correction: Store an absolute game-time expiry or decrement from an elapsed tick/time event, with the documented tick-rate assumption removed or verified.
findings.smallest_regression_test: After a successful fracture, advance the real mocked game clock by ten seconds without firing weapon-hit events, then fire one correctly ordered hit and assert the hook is eligible to roll again.
